_comment: PERF-MISS-1104-TRACE / OD-1104-TRACE: per-request diagnostic trace (vera/request_trace.py). The question text is kept owner-only and purged after 30 days by an owner-run script (work/PERF-MISS-1104/trace/purge_trace.sh). The request id is owner-visible only: response header X-VERA-Trace-Id, logs and the DB, never the UI.
_calibration: PROVISIONAL size bounds, not decision thresholds (nothing is accepted or rejected by them; they only cap diagnostic payloads). No live trace data exists yet. max_events_per_request 400: today's closed progress stage set is about 10 stages x 2 providers plus up to 31 inline ACQUIRE updates (progress.json note), so 400 leaves room for the planned wiring events; the finish event is always kept. max_detail_bytes 2048 / max_str_chars 200 / max_list_items 20: a detail holds ids, scores and reason codes, never text. max_question_chars 4000: equals AskRequest.question max_length (main.py), so nothing valid is cut. recent_max 50 / recent_ttl_s 900: owner route window only. queue_max 5000, batch_max 200, flush_interval_s 2: one background writer; a full queue drops rows (counted), it never blocks a request. Data that would change them: dropped-row counters, events per request seen in the first week of vera_trace log lines.

log_sink._comment: include_question ships FALSE pending owner decision: host logs cannot be purged by purge_trace.sh (so the About page's 30-day promise would not hold for them) and the existing R-028 tests (test_ask_progress_api, test_disclosure_persistence) assert the question never reaches logs. While false the start line carries question_chars only; the full text is in the owner route /trace/request/{id} (recent window) and, once 015 is applied, the DB.

db_sink._comment: ON since 2026-11-04: the owner applied migration 015 (db/migrations/pending/015-DRAFT-request-trace.sql.draft; owner-reported, verify output not seen by agents). App-path INSERT only, write-only account. request_trace.db_view (read through db_url_env_ro) exists and is tested but is wired to the owner route only while db_sink.owner_route_db_view is true (default false, DEFERRED-DB-1104); 015 grants vera_vjay_ro no SELECT on the trace tables, so it needs an owner-read login named in the optional key db_url_env_owner_read (work/DEFERRED-DB-1104/grant_trace_read.sh).

retention_purge._comment: PURGE-WIRING-1105: daily in-app purge of trace rows older than 30 days by calling vera_vjay.purge_expired_trace() (migration 018; owner approval needed) on the wo account via vera/retention_purge.py from the trace writer thread. Enabled per owner decision OD-1105-PURGE-ENABLE (2026-11-05); it needs migration 018 applied and fails closed without it. While enabled is false no connection is opened. Needs db_sink.enabled. interval_s 86400 = once a day; initial_delay_s 300 = first run 5 min after the writer starts and the first retry delay (doubles on error, capped at interval_s); statement_timeout_ms 60000 because the flush engine's 2000 is too short for a bulk delete (PROVISIONAL: no live row counts exist; data that would change it: rows deleted and run time in the first week of 'vera_trace purge' log lines).

digest_store._comment: Latest corpus digest persisted in the DB (owner rule: runtime state lives in the DB). Table exists since migration 015 (2026-11-04, owner-reported) and this flag is ON since DEFERRED-DB-1104 (2026-11-04). When true, vera/corpus_description.py reuses the stored digest for the same corpus state and prompt version after a restart and saves each new digest (code + offline tests in place). Write: write-only account (INSERT). Read: read-only account (SELECT).

key_allowlist._comment: DENYALL-TRACE-1104 (owner standard 2026-11-04: Deny All; approve specified exceptions-from-Deny). Event detail keys are stored only if listed here for the event's stage; others are dropped and counted in detail.dropped_keys. A missing stage lists nothing (all detail keys dropped). String values must also fullmatch ^[a-z0-9_:.-]{1,64}$ else '<str>' (request_trace.py). Keys inside nested maps (codes, ms, per_claim items, acquisition) are limited to identifier tokens. Question text is never allowed in any stage; it is stored only in the requests table question column (OD-1104-TRACE). Derived from every rt.event / _rt_event call site in vera/ on 2026-11-04. Adding a key requires a reason here. Optional 'nested' maps a key to the allowed keys inside its mapping; keys without an entry (codes, ms) accept identifier-token keys only.

start.reason: start event carries no detail; client id and endpoint go to the log line / requests row only

finish.reason: terminal event: closed message code from request_trace.finish

acquire.reason: inline_acquire._trace_done, ask_service acquire/outcome/candidate/answer_fallback/off/retry_skipped: status, reason-code counts (codes), phase ms, per-candidate provider/outcome/reason/diag tokens, nested acquisition summary, lanes flag, fallback token. 'reason' also used by off and retry_skipped events.

lane.reason: PERF-MISS-1105-FIX2 F2 inline_acquire._trace_lane: the lane pass portal token (gdelt, hn or -), called/skipped, a closed reason token (ok, no_items, outlet_policy, circuit, spacing, throttled, failed, http_4xx, off, no_terms, no_reporting_part, error) and the news-intent flag; item/page/link counts are counts. Never a URL, outlet, title or question text. H19-FIX-1109 (design section 8, T6): acc_exc_first = the first page-check exception token of vera.page_licence (closed set: acc_page_licence_mismatch, page_licence_reject, acc_republished, acc_item_excluded, acc_third_party_page, acc_third_party_ambiguous, acc_third_party_all, acc_third_party_config, acc_licence_unset, page_check_error); nd_read, nd_link_only, page_link_only, acc_exc and a11_drop are counts.

reading_list.reason: PERF-MISS-1105-FIX2 F4 ask_service._reading_list start/done: counts only (candidates)

search.reason: search_and_fetch and search_providers: provider name, status and latency per provider/portal/seed fallback

premise.reason: fulldoc_answer premise check: verdict token and whether the reason cited a source

passages.reason: fulldoc_answer: span ids and relevance scores sent to the writer / cited; ids and numbers only, never text

writer.reason: fulldoc_answer writer draft/fall: fallback token, model id, cost

claim_check.reason: claim_check: checker label, exception class name, per-claim id/verdict/cites (nested keys id, verdict, cites). H19-FIX-1109 (design section 8, T6): nd_guard_rule = the first nd_guard rule that dropped a sentence (closed set: closed, g9, g1, g2g3, g10, g4, g5, none); nd_guard_drop and nd_<rule> are counts.

scope.reason: ask_service scope gate: basis, layer and class tokens, accepted flag, refusal token

outcome.reason: ask_service outcome events: decline category, fallback token, branch, cause, inline status

query_norm.reason: A-P1-NORM-1107 vera/query_norm.py: mode (off|shadow|on), the LLM-step status code (not_needed|disabled|cooldown|exhausted|busy|no_client|rate_limited|error|timeout|rejected|ok) and a latency bucket code (lt100|lt500|lt1000|lt2500|lt5000|ge5000); counts (det, llm, vouched terms) go in counts. Never the question or any term text.

purpose_grant.reason: PURPOSE-GRANTS-1108 vera/purpose_grants.shadow: shadow record of what a site-owner purpose grant would do to a restriction. Code is the decision (would_admit|review|negated|not_overridable); detail holds closed tokens only: mode, restriction reason code, why token, channel (robots_comment|robots_field|http_header|tdmrep), grant kind, purpose and condition names joined by ':', and a list of 16-hex evidence ids. Never the verbatim text, URL or host: those stay in the owner-only in-process ring keyed by evidence id.

multiq.reason: MULTIQ-1108 vera/ask_service.py _multiq/_answer_parts: shape (multi_question|multi_part|single), mode (off|shadow|on) and a part's result_kind (closed enum); counts (parts, over_cap, pronoun_carry, part) go in counts. Never the question or any part text. Calibration of max_questions reads these counts.
